# SteamLite 10.1.5

A new Non-Steam page.

- New Non-Steam button in the dock: it lists the games that are running right now and are not from Steam. SteamLite spots them from the running programs (what Task Manager shows), by their window, DirectX or Vulkan use, game engine and anti-cheat files, and where they are installed, including games with an anti-cheat.
- Each game gets pictures and details looked up for it: first from the Steam store (many games sold elsewhere are on Steam too), then Wikipedia, then the program's own icon.
- Click a game for a temporary game page with its art, developer, genres, how long it has been running and why SteamLite thinks it is a game. The game is not kept in your library and the page goes away when the game closes. Add to library keeps it (with its picture), and Show file location opens its folder.
- Games from a store's launcher now say so: on the game page of a game from Rockstar, Epic, GOG, EA, Ubisoft, Battle.net, Riot or Xbox, Play becomes Open Rockstar Games Launcher (or whichever it is). SteamLite works out the launcher from where the game is installed, the files next to it and who made it, opens it, and keeps watching for the game so your play time is still counted (for up to 15 minutes after you open the launcher). If that launcher is not installed, Play works as before.
- Only the name of a game is sent out, to look up its pictures. Programs and file locations stay on your PC.
- With ten buttons the dock shrinks a little on short windows so they all fit.
